what_happened: The first version of reduceChain applied a single last-write-wins rule to every setFact/relocate, keyed by (subject, predicate) cell. For the history [setFact(S,P,"V1"), retractFact(F), setFact(S,P,"V2")] where the writes are ILLEGAL, the reduction dropped the first write. The differential harness caught a real semantic divergence: the legacy world carried the contradiction record for "V1" while the incremental world carried the record for "V2".
root_cause: A rejected fact write never enters buildModel.overriddenCells — it is recorded in rejectedFactWrites and rendered as a `fact-write-illegal` contradiction. That contradiction's record id is `contra:<subject>:fact-write-illegal:<reason>`, which does NOT include the written value, so detectContradictions keeps the FIRST such write per id. Last-write-wins is therefore the wrong subsumption rule for rejected writes; the correct rule is first-wins-per-contradiction-id.
what_i_did_wrong: Reasoned about the write fold purely in terms of the effective-fact cell (last-write-wins) and missed that rejected writes take a completely different path into the semantic state (the contradictions dimension). The reduction was written from the effective-fact semantics alone.
detection: Adversarial matrix case `write+retract+write[fact/kael-oath-is-oath]` (dimension=facts) reported semantic=false, hash=false, diff=false while throwEqual=true. Isolated with experiments/s008/debug-case.ts.
fix: Split setFact/relocate reduction by legality. Legal writes keep LAST per cell. Rejected writes (factAssertionError != null) keep FIRST per `contra:<subject>:fact-write-illegal:<reason>`. The reduction now reuses factAssertionError + buildFactVocabulary (the same validation the engine uses), so the two paths cannot disagree about what counts as rejected.
verification: After the fix, matrix went 296/297 -> 297/297 (verrin) and the full run reached 1632/1632 differential cases across both canons.
lesson: When reducing a fold, enumerate EVERY path an element can take into the semantic state, not just the primary one. Rejected/invalid inputs often have their own accumulation rule (here: first-per-id) that differs from the valid-input rule (last-per-write). The differential harness is what turned a plausible-looking reduction into a caught defect.
